TechnologyStack.Framework: Go HTTP API, PostgreSQL, MinIO, Redis/asynq, Python workers, CopperASR runtime submodule, React Web UI, Telegram adapter, MCP adapter

ArchitectureShape.goal: Make the API the durable product authority for media accumulation, curation, execution, artifacts, diagnostics, channel recovery, idempotency, and retention.
ArchitectureShape.canonical-chain: media_asset -> collection/inbox -> immutable selection_snapshot -> analysis_run -> analysis_run_step/artifacts -> artifact_subject lineage
ArchitectureShape.control-plane: Go API owns target public contracts, channel_account scope, lifecycle transitions, validation, operation_requests, retention policy, diagnostics, artifact metadata, and channel_surface recovery state.
ArchitectureShape.execution-plane: Python workers consume sealed selection_snapshot material and declared analysis_run_step_inputs through internal execution contracts.
ArchitectureShape.queue-plane: Redis/asynq remains an execution transport only; queued work does not define user-facing product concepts.
ArchitectureShape.object-plane: MinIO stores stored_object bodies for media assets, previews, generated artifacts, private execution evidence, and diagnostic bundles behind API-issued access decisions.
ArchitectureShape.adapters: Telegram, Web, and MCP are thin clients over the same API-owned media_asset, collection, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, diagnostic, channel_account, and channel_surface state.

component.role: Go HTTP API, WebSocket server, storage orchestrator, and channel-account-scoped product authority
Pinned CopperASR source submodule for the dedicated ASR runtime service
Python report and research execution behind analysis_run_steps
React management UI for inbox, collections, selections, runs, artifacts, and diagnostics
Thin Telegram capture, rendering, and recovery adapter over API-owned state
Thin MCP tool adapter over API-owned state
OpenAPI and JSON schema source for target vocabulary plus explicit deprecated compatibility contracts

table.name: channel_accounts
table.purpose: Durable external channel identities for the single human user.
table.fields: id, channel, external_account_ref, display_name, status, metadata, created_at, updated_at, last_seen_at, disabled_at
table.rules: Channel accounts are access and recovery scope, not product owners or workspaces.

table.name: operation_requests
table.purpose: Idempotency and audit records for accepted mutating channel operations.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, operation_type, idempotency_key, request_hash, status, target_type, target_id, error_code, metadata, created_at, completed_at
table.rules: Retries must be deterministic and conflict-aware.

table.name: stored_objects
table.purpose: Shared object storage metadata for input media and output artifacts.
table.fields: id, bucket, object_key, content_type, size_bytes, checksum, storage_status, retention_state, created_at, expires_at, deleted_at
table.rules: Stored object lifecycle can expire bytes without deleting historical run metadata.

table.name: media_assets
table.purpose: Channel-account-scoped durable input records independent of execution.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, stored_object_id, origin_type, origin_ref, kind, display_name, status, metadata, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
table.rules: Accepted media assets land in inbox by default; invalid assets remain visible through diagnostics.

table.name: collections
table.purpose: Mutable channel-account-scoped groups, including the default inbox.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, kind, name, status, version, created_at, updated_at, archived_at, deleted_at
table.rules: Collection membership is mutable and version checked; collection edits never mutate sealed snapshots.

table.name: collection_items
table.purpose: Ordered membership between collections and media_asset records.
table.fields: id, collection_id, media_asset_id, position, added_via_channel_account_id, added_at, removed_at
table.rules: Active membership has unique asset and position constraints per collection.

table.name: selection_snapshots
table.purpose: Immutable ordered snapshots prepared for analysis.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, source_collection_id, status, option_snapshot, diagnostics, created_via_channel_account_id, created_at, sealed_at
table.rules: Selection snapshots are never recomputed from later collection state and storage rejects direct update/delete attempts.

table.name: selection_snapshot_items
table.purpose: Frozen item facts consumed by workers.
table.fields: id, selection_snapshot_id, position, media_asset_id, kind, display_name, origin_snapshot, storage_snapshot, metadata_snapshot, status_at_selection, diagnostics
table.rules: Workers read snapshot facts, not mutable collection rows.

table.name: analysis_runs
table.purpose: User-facing execution records created from selection_snapshots.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, selection_snapshot_id, run_type, status, version, idempotency_key, params, delivery, evidence_gate_state, created_via_channel_account_id, created_at, started_at, completed_at, cancel_requested_at, canceled_at, expires_at
table.rules: Public clients address analysis_run; internal steps remain behind it.

table.name: analysis_run_steps
table.purpose: Internal worker-visible step, claim, heartbeat, retry, and finalization state.
table.fields: id, analysis_run_id, step_kind, worker_kind, status, attempt_no, lease_owner, claimed_at, heartbeat_at, finalized_at, metadata, created_at
table.rules: Steps are internal execution records, not public product objects.

table.name: analysis_run_step_inputs
table.purpose: Declared immutable inputs a worker step may read.
table.fields: id, analysis_run_step_id, input_kind, selection_snapshot_item_id, artifact_id, position, required, metadata, created_at
table.rules: Report and research steps consume transcript/text-corpus artifacts when speech prerequisites exist; active worker code materializes declared artifact inputs instead of discovering raw speech media.

table.name: analysis_run_events
table.purpose: Append-only run status, artifact, and diagnostic timeline.
table.fields: id, analysis_run_id, event_type, version, status, payload, created_at
table.rules: Events power polling and WebSocket updates.

table.name: artifacts
table.purpose: Run outputs, previews, evidence objects, and downloadable files.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, analysis_run_id, stored_object_id, kind, status, content_type, checksum, size_bytes, visibility, preview, created_at, expires_at, deleted_at
table.rules: Artifact access is mediated by the API and scoped through channel_account plus run; worker-published artifacts create stored_object metadata and artifact_subject lineage.

table.name: artifact_subjects
table.purpose: Lineage links from artifacts to runs, steps, snapshots, selected items, media assets, or diagnostics.
table.fields: id, artifact_id, subject_type, subject_id, subject_role, created_at
table.rules: Lineage removes guessing from worker and UI artifact resolution.

table.name: diagnostics
table.purpose: Structured failure, warning, and operator evidence for target subjects.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, subject_type, subject_id, severity, code, message, context, safe_channel_context, correlation_id, remediation_hint, created_at
table.rules: Rejected records and partial failures are represented as diagnostics, not hidden drops.

table.name: channel_surfaces
table.purpose: Restart-safe external presentation mappings for Telegram, Web recovery surfaces, or future channels.
table.fields: id, channel_account_id, channel, surface_type, surface_key, address, address_fingerprint, display_state, lifecycle_status, version, idempotency_key, created_at, updated_at, last_rendered_at, superseded_at, deleted_at
table.rules: Channel surfaces cannot drive product lifecycle.

table.name: channel_surface_subjects
table.purpose: Links from channel surfaces to represented product or diagnostic subjects.
table.rules: One primary subject per surface is allowed.

table.name: channel_surface_events
table.purpose: Append-only operational history for channel surface recovery and delivery investigations.
table.fields: id, surface_id, event_type, reason, previous_version, next_version, actor_type, actor_id, metadata, created_at
table.rules: Delivery failures remain channel evidence and do not mutate product entities.

CompatibilitySurface.deprecated: Maps media_item/source/owner fields to media_asset/origin/stored_object/channel_account during transition only.
Maps selection_id and media_item_id fields to selection_snapshot_id and media_asset_id during transition only.
Maps only to internal analysis_run_step migration concepts and must not appear in target public contracts.

LifecycleAndRetention.status-source: Lifecycle statuses are defined in docs/requirements.xml and mirrored in packages/contracts schemas.
LifecycleAndRetention.retention-rule: Soft-deleted media_assets and collection membership are hidden from default reads but retained until policy permits hard deletion.
Selection snapshots remain immutable audit snapshots even if stored object bodies later expire.
Artifacts can expire independently from run metadata; diagnostics explain unavailable artifacts.
Deletion and export workflows must include media_asset, stored_object, collection, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, artifact_subject, diagnostic, and channel_surface records.

AsrRuntime.contract: media-analysis-platform owns queues, media_assets, selection_snapshots, analysis_runs, progress, cancellation, artifacts, diagnostics, and channel surfaces. CopperASR owns ASR model lifecycle, inference, sanitized ASR errors, /health, and /transcribe.
AsrRuntime.artifact-contract: TranscriptResult carries provider_metadata so run_manifest can identify CopperASR provider, model, duration, and sanitized runtime metadata while visible transcript artifacts remain plain text, markdown, and DOCX.
AsrRuntime.target-topology: Dedicated internal CopperASR HTTP runtime service consumed by workers/transcription through COPPER_ASR_BASE_URL.
AsrRuntime.dependency-policy: Root Python dependencies stay free of removed legacy ASR packages; CopperASR runtime dependencies are isolated in the dedicated image and submodule runtime.
AsrRuntime.cleanup-policy: Legacy ASR imports, model-conversion helpers, provider-specific env, old model-cache volumes, fallback tests, and dual-backend switches are removed and must not remain active fallback behavior.
AsrRuntime.guardrail: Active runtime, compose, env, dependency manifest, and doc surfaces must continue to reject removed ASR runtime reintroduction outside historical research or migration plans.
AsrRuntime.verification-ref: media-b8s.1.4, media-b8s.1.5, media-b8s.1.6, media-b8s.1.7, media-b8s.1.8, media-b8s.1.9, media-b8s.1.10, media-b8s.2.5, media-b8s.3.1

AdapterContracts.telegram: Telegram captures input, resolves channel_account scope, creates media_assets, shows inbox or collection state, creates selection_snapshots, starts analysis_run records, persists current_materials_panel, analysis_task_surface, and result_artifact_surface channel_surfaces, recovers active surfaces after restart, and sends artifact previews or downloads returned by the API. Result deduplication requires a valid Telegram surface address; stale addressless result surfaces are superseded and delivery is retried.
AdapterContracts.web: Web provides management UI for materials, groups, selections, progress, results, downloads, errors, and retention over target public API contracts. Service ASR metadata from run_manifest remains hidden from normal human result views.
AdapterContracts.mcp: MCP exposes stable tools over the same API and never maintains its own durable media store. MCP artifact preview tools can return CopperASR run_manifest metadata for explicit service artifact reads.

EvidenceContracts.contract-evidence: Schema tests must prove target DTOs and route names exist, deprecated compatibility is isolated, and stale public product vocabulary does not appear in target operations.
EvidenceContracts.storage-evidence: Storage tests must cover target migration fragments, absence of legacy target tables, channel_account isolation, immutable selection snapshots, operation_request idempotency, step input linkage, lifecycle transitions, retention, diagnostics, channel_surface supersede rules, and artifact_subject lineage.
EvidenceContracts.api-evidence: API tests must cover ingestion, inbox membership, collection mutation, selection_snapshot sealing, analysis_run creation, prerequisite planning, event polling, cancellation, worker artifact stored_object registration, artifact access, and diagnostics queries.
EvidenceContracts.worker-evidence: Worker tests must cover step_kind queue polling, analysis_run_step claim/progress/finalize, sealed selection_snapshot consumption, declared artifact step input materialization, API-safe diagnostic identifiers, partial diagnostics, and cancellation.
EvidenceContracts.asr-evidence: ASR evidence must cover CopperASR HTTP client configuration, service health, transcript artifact publication, sanitized provider metadata in run_manifest, stable asr_* diagnostics, hidden provider internals in normal Telegram/Web surfaces, explicit MCP service artifact previews, compose topology, and no-legacy runtime guardrails.
EvidenceContracts.adapter-evidence: Adapter tests must prove Telegram, Web, and MCP operate over the same API-owned state and do not expose grouped submission modes as durable product state. Telegram tests must also prove target channel_account media_asset, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, and diagnostic request shapes plus channel_surface restart recovery, result duplicate prevention, and supersede behavior.
EvidenceContracts.runtime-evidence: Runtime smoke must prove a real item can be ingested, selected, analyzed, and resolved as artifacts with diagnostics available for failures.
